analysis:
The PR bumps the landing site's Next.js dependency from 16.2.6 to 16.4.1 in landing/package.json (line 13) and regenerates landing/package-lock.json. The lockfile changes include sharp 0.34.5 to 0.35.5 with libvips 1.3.4, plus engine floor changes. The visible lockfile tail (lines 3921-4159) shows only dev-only transitive entries such as tough-cookie, undici and typescript, all with registry.npmjs.org resolved URLs and sha512 integrity hashes. I saw no git/http URLs, missing integrity fields or install scripts in the visible portions. The lockfile patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the lockfile diff was not fully reviewed. Only the final tail excerpt and the patch head were visible.

The change touches only the marketing landing site build, outside the provider and native-runtime threat model scope (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 and so on). It does not touch the provider process, the coordinator WebSocket contract, attestation, keys, authorization or cache storage. No provider or consumer data path, trust boundary or mitigation is affected. No finding qualifies.

Remaining unverified points: the new Next 16.4.1 release contents and the middle of the lockfile diff (about lines 626-1663 in head) were not visible. The sharp engine floor moved to node >=20.9.0, so build or CI Node versions must satisfy it. This is an availability and build concern, not a security regression. @next/eslint-plugin-next stays at 16.2.6, a version mismatch that is non-security. The lockfile appears to be a standard npm regeneration.
